verified_against_binary: v2.36.1 RETRACTS two claims published in v2.36.0 and restores a fact that release wrongly rewrote. Root cause: v2.36.0 treated the Desktop's per-session audit.jsonl as the authoritative first-party record. It is a TRANSLATED PROJECTION -- across the whole on-disk corpus, 16,640 tool_use ids appear in both audit.jsonl and the agent's own transcript under .claude/projects/; 757 inputs differ, and 100% of the differences are audit '/Users/...' versus transcript '/sessions/...'. There is no other kind of difference. RETRACTED (1): the read-after-write race. The two Read calls that looked byte-identical in audit.jsonl were, in the agent's own transcript, a VM-form path (denied) followed by a host-form path (succeeded) -- two different calls behaving exactly as documented. No race, no index lag, no retry to perform. RETRACTED (2): inbound host->VM path translation. The agent sent 'echo hello-K4M2 > /sessions/busy-eager-bell/mnt/outputs/k4m2.txt' -- the VM form. It never sent a host path. Ch35/L122's 'rewrites outbound messages only' STANDS; v2.36.0's correction of it is withdrawn. RESTORED: paths.session-paths-denied, whose original wording was correct. v2.36.0 replaced it with 'retry, do not rewrite the path', which would have sent an author into an unbounded retry loop -- the Desktop gate is a pure prefix test (i === '/sessions' || i.startsWith('/sessions/')), one site, identical across app.asar 1.22209.0 / 1.24012.1 / 1.25927.0, absent from the agent bundles, and reached from two call sites that both pass the RAW tool input. A '/Users/' path cannot reach that branch, which is what proved the record wrong. UNAFFECTED: L145 (installs succeed; the finding is about pip and npm, not path form) and L146. Chapter 40's L143 and L144 are rewritten around the two-record distinction; its methodology note now says plainly that 'first-party' is not a synonym for 'authoritative' -- ask what the artifact is for. The audit log speaks in host paths by design, because it exists to show a human what happened.
